items.title: Stock picks of the week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 31%
items.description: When the Indian market will start to recover in any real sense is still an open question. But one positive is that the broader market indices have been able to weather the storm called the US-Iran war much better than most expected. This suggests that the probability and possibility of a sharp correction is low. Our selected stocks for today depict a strong upward trajectory in their overall average score which is based on five key pillars: Earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum. This implies that there has been a significant improvement in their market outlook in the given time frame.

items.title: Vedanta, Wipro among 10 stocks that saw biggest jump in retail holders in Q1. See full list
items.description: Retail investor participation in the Indian equity markets continues to demonstrate strong momentum, with millions of individual investors expanding their presence across key sectors. In the first quarter of the financial year, several prominent listed companies recorded a substantial increase in their retail shareholder base, reflecting heightened interest in major market players. Here are top 10 stocks with highest increase in retail participation.

items.title: We imported the auction, but we left out the brakes
items.description: India’s Closing Auction Session (CAS) was introduced to improve price discovery, but recent sharp swings have exposed gaps in its safeguards. Jimeet Modi argues that allowing order cancellations until the auction ends can leave markets vulnerable to manipulation, calling for stronger controls, deeper liquidity and better protection around index-level settlement prices.

items.title: Vanguard’s India Portfolio: 12 stocks surge up to 190% in CY26; 3 multibaggers, 3 new entrants
items.description: Vanguard Fund’s portfolio is making a strong statement in the Indian equity market — and the numbers speak for themselves. Ranked among the top three active foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the country, Vanguard has built a substantial portfolio of Indian equities through its global funds. As of August 28, 2026, the value of its holdings in 47 BSE-listed companies stood at an impressive Rs 96,715 crore, based on June 2026 quarter shareholding data. This represents a sharp 46% increase from Rs 66,403 crore in the December 2025 quarter.A recent ETMarkets analysis shows that 11 key stocks in Vanguard’s portfolio have delivered returns ranging from 25% to 190% so far in CY26, with three emerging as multibaggers. The analysis also highlights three stocks that were newly added to Vanguard’s portfolio during the March 2026 quarter. (Data Source: ACE Equity, Trendlyne)

items.title: Indian bank stocks show widest exchange price gap in decades
items.description: Indian bank stocks saw unusually wide price gaps between the NSE and BSE during Thursday’s closing auction, with IndusInd Bank recording its widest exchange price difference in more than two decades. The divergence has intensified scrutiny of the new auction system amid thin liquidity, monthly expiry pressures and concerns over market manipulation.

items.title: Concurrent Gainers: 13 smallcap stocks that gain for 5 days in a row, surge up to 45%
items.description: Over the five trading sessions ending August 28, the Sensex benchmark declined 0.36%, or 276 points, to close at 77,264, falling in three of the five sessions. Despite the broader market decline, around 35 stocks from the BSE SmallCap index advanced in each of the five consecutive sessions between August 24 and 28. Of these, 13 smallcap stocks posted gains on all five days, delivering cumulative returns of between 10% and 45% during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Bajaj Finance, L&T Finance poised to benefit as NBFC earnings recovery broadens: Siddhartha Khemka
items.description: India’s NBFC sector is showing signs of a broad-based cyclical recovery, with FY27 first-quarter results pointing to stronger loan growth, improving asset quality, lower credit costs and emerging operating leverage. Earnings estimates are also being upgraded, raising expectations of sustained profitability and a potential valuation re-rating across leading lenders.

items.title: BSE, Hindustan Zinc among 5 stocks with revenue growth of up to 64% in 1 year. Check details
items.description: Five key stocks, including BSE and Muthoot Finance, recorded strong revenue growth over the past year, with gains of up to 64%. Here is the detailed breakdown, based on data reported by ET Wealth as of August 20, 2026.

items.title: Tech leads D-Street bound, FPI play in focus
items.description: On Friday, Indian equities bounced back, driven predominantly by a surge in technology stocks. Investors showed renewed interest in undervalued IT shares, aided by a decline in crude oil prices. After a prolonged period of selling, foreign investors reversed their trend, becoming net buyers in July and August. Broader market indices also benefited from this trend, as mid and small-cap stocks appreciated.

items.title: Nearly half of BSE 200 stocks fail to deliver returns in 2026. What’s dragging them down?
items.description: This year, numerous firms across various sectors are grappling with a lack of returns, a stark contrast to the previous years' performances. Key industries such as automobiles, FMCG, and IT are showing marked declines. Interestingly, capital goods stocks have demonstrated resilience, fueled by increased infrastructure spending. This downturn in the market parallels a slowdown in systematic investment plan inflows.

items.title: Suzlon, Tata Motors among 10 stocks that saw sharpest drop in retail shareholders in Q1. Own any?
items.description: Retail investors trimmed their exposure to several widely held Indian stocks in the June quarter, with shareholder counts falling sharply across sectors. The decline comes as market volatility, stock-specific developments and shifting investor preferences reshape retail portfolios. Here are the 10 companies that saw the steepest drop in retail shareholders

items.title: Sebi bars Trafiksol ITS, its promoters from securities market for 1 year; slaps Rs 1.05 cr fine
items.description: Sebi has taken decisive action against Trafiksol and its promoters, imposing a one-year ban from the securities market. The company and its directors face penalties totaling Rs 1.05 crore after being found in serious breach of regulations concerning financial disclosures and the allocation of IPO funds. The decision comes in light of complaints regarding Trafiksol's SME IPO, which was significantly oversubscribed at a rate of 345.

items.title: MCX logs record daily turnover of Rs 62.93 lakh crore amid strong activity
items.description: MCX recorded its highest-ever daily turnover of Rs 62.93 lakh crore on August 28, driven largely by options activity across more than 3.13 crore contracts. The record comes as the exchange strengthens its physical-derivatives market linkage through standardised delivery norms, supporting greater participation, hedging and depth in commodity markets.
